stage1.impression: A rim-lit coloured armillary globe on a black drum at a canal quay at night. The globe and its coloured shadow are a real idea, but the frame reads as a clean render. A huge uniform white spotlight disc with a hard stage edge takes up the lower half, the paving is spotless and tiled, the facade across the water is a flat dark slab with identical square windows (an office block, not Amsterdam canal houses), and the plinth is a featureless black blob. A jury would see a specific, striking object but a generic render of a generic place, not this work on an Amsterdam gracht.

blocking_9: The hard spot's pool must stop dominating the frame: paving under it no more than about 2.5x the frame median, and the cone tightened so it frames the globe and its shadow rather than lighting half the quay with a theatrical elliptical cut-off
The far bank must read as Amsterdam: gabled brick canal houses of varied widths and heights, windows with frames, glazing bars and varied warm interiors, not one flat block of identical squares
The quay must read as worn real stone or klinker brick at 1:1, with varied tones, joints, grime and wet gloss, not uniform clean CG tiles
The blackened-steel plinth must show its form (a soft sheen on its top edge and a rim highlight) instead of a crushed black cylinder
Some sign of place and life: a bicycle against a bollard, a far figure, a moored boat, so it reads as a photograph on the canals
One coherent colour of light: the spot currently paints the paving neutral-cool grey while the street lamps are deep orange; they should belong to the same night

defects.what: The spotlight pool is a huge, flat, evenly lit ellipse (median 119, p95 157) with a hard stage-like edge; it reads as a theatre follow-spot and takes up the lower third of the frame
The paving is clean, uniform, repeating grey tiles with no wear, staining, wetness or variation; it reads as CG at 1:1
The far facade is one flat dark block with identical square windows lit in two flat tones, with no gables, brick, frames or interiors; it does not read as Amsterdam
The plinth is crushed (median 12.8, p95 59) with no visible sheen, edge highlight or steel patina; it reads as a black prop cylinder
The water on the right is crushed (median 5.6) and featureless apart from the window reflections; no ripple texture or sky gloss
The street lamp is a generic lantern on a thin pole with an empty dark quay around it; there is no context to tie it to the site
Inside the coloured shadow a dark, blade-like shape cut by the axis and hub reads as an artefact; the coloured overlaps are pleasing but slightly muddy (r76 g46 b38)
The rims are fine, but the clear faces show little reflection or edge glow at the slots; the globe interior reads as dark smoked glass rather than clear acrylic
No people, bicycles, boats or other props: an empty set

changes.problem: The hard spot lights far too much of the quay too evenly, so the frame reads as a stage and the coloured shadow is just one feature inside a big white disc.

evidence.measured: lum_median 119 (about 4x the frame median of 29.6); a uniform plateau of 142 across y 600 to 740, then a drop over about 75 px at the cone edge

change.setting: the hard spot: power and cone
change.to: 380 W, cone 20 deg with a soft edge (blend 0.35), aimed at [0.9, -2.4, 0.0] so the pool holds the plinth and the shadow and fades before the bottom of the frame

changes.expected: A smaller, softer-edged pool that frames the globe and its shadow; the lower foreground falls into darkness, and the shadow becomes the brightest-contrast motif on the ground

changes.problem: The spot paints the paving neutral-cool grey while the lamps are deep orange, so the light is not one coherent night.

evidence.measured: r126 g117 b116 under the spot vs r80 g50 b27 under the lamp at [0,330,300,560]

change.to: spot at 3000 K, white balance 3400 K

changes.expected: The pool turns a warm stone colour (r roughly 15 to 25 above b), the lamps stay amber but less orange, and the coloured shadow keeps its hues against a warm, not grey, ground

changes.problem: The paving is uniform clean tiling that reads as CG and not as an Amsterdam quay.

evidence.measured: Seen at 1:1: identical grey tiles with fine noise and no colour variation, wear, staining or wetness

change.to: red-brown Dutch klinker brick in herringbone or stretcher bond, per-brick tone variation of plus or minus 15 %, dark sanded joints, grime toward the kerb, and damp patches at roughness 0.25 to 0.35 so the spot and lamps leave soft glints; a granite kerb at the water's edge

changes.expected: A ground that reads as a real Amsterdam quay after rain, with highlights that break up the pool and give it texture

changes.problem: The far bank is a flat dark slab of identical square windows, not canal houses, so the place is generic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 13.3; windows in two flat tones, no gables or brick visible at 1:1

change.setting: the houses across (materials' finish, windows lit and glow)
change.from: one uniform facade, 0.45 of the windows lit at glow 0.18
change.to: a row of narrow brick canal houses with varied widths, step, neck and bell gables, white window frames with glazing bars; 0.3 of the windows lit at glow 0.12 to 0.25 with varied warm interiors (2400 to 3000 K) and some curtains; brick at albedo about 0.18 with a faint far-quay fill so the facades hold detail

changes.expected: The background reads as an Amsterdam gracht at once, and the reflections in the water become varied warm streaks

changes.problem: The plinth is crushed to a black blob with no sign of blackened steel.

change.setting: the plinth's finish (materials' finish of the quay props)
change.to: blackened steel, base colour about #1C1A18, metallic 1.0, roughness 0.45 with low-frequency variation, faint brownish patina, and a crisp eased top edge that catches the spot

changes.expected: A soft sheen along the top rim and the lit side; the drum reads as steel while staying near black

changes.problem: The quay is empty, with no sign of life or place, so it reads as a set.

evidence.measured: Seen: no bicycles, people, boats or benches; only two bollards and one lamp

change.to: a black Dutch bicycle leaning on the right bollard at about [3.0, -1.2]; one or two figures, softly out of focus, on the far quay; a moored low sloep at the far bank; Amsterdammertje bollards (brown-red with the three crosses) in place of the plain ones

changes.expected: Scale and life; a jury reads 'Amsterdam canals' at a glance

changes.problem: The water and the dark areas are crushed, and the air is too clean, so the night has no atmosphere and the spot beam is invisible.

change.setting: haze and the water's ripple and gloss
change.from: haze 0.0025 per m; water near mirror, flat
change.to: haze 0.006 per m (enough that the spot's beam just shows); water ripple normal amplitude up by about 1.5x, roughness 0.05, with a faint sky reflection; sky strength 0.12 to 0.18

changes.expected: The water holds a deep blue-grey gloss with broken reflection streaks, and a faint shaft from the mast ties the shadow to its source

changes.problem: The globe's clear faces read as dark smoked glass and the rims are only modest, so the hero does not glow as much as the shadow is lit.

evidence.measured: lum_median 21.1, p95 177.6, clip 0.89 %; the faces inside the rims are as dark as the water behind

change.to: 0.2, with a faint scatter in the acrylic so the slots and face edges catch a little of the rim light

changes.expected: The rims become the brightest coloured lines in the frame without blowing out, and the faces show faint coloured edge glow and clean reflections of the windows

out_of_scope.request: The dark, blade-shaped shadow of the axis and hub inside the coloured shadow could be softened or shortened
out_of_scope.why: It comes from the globe's fixed design and the spot's position; only the spot's aim may change it, and changing the design is not allowed

out_of_scope.request: Tinted faces, so the coloured shadow would be stronger
out_of_scope.why: Clear faces with rim lighting are fixed by the card
